transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because for the past few weeks, I've just felt this... this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me pretty much all day. Even when I'm at work and I'm smiling at my patients, inside I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
How many weeks exactly have you been feeling this way?
It's been about three weeks now. It started... well, shortly after I found out I was pregnant.
Have you noticed any decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy since you've been feeling this way?

Yeah, I have. Usually, after my shifts, I used to paint, or go to yoga or salsa dancing to decompress. But lately, I just go straight home and sit on the couch. I've been ignoring texts from people, too, because... I don't know, none of it really feels worth the effort anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you've been moving since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, I have. It's like... everything I do just feels slowed down. Honestly, it feels like I'm moving through syrup. Even simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound supplies or finishing up my charting, they take me noticeably longer than they should.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself since you started feeling this way?

Well, that's actually what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment. I've been having these thoughts... like I just wish I wouldn't wake up. I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that, but the thoughts are there, and they really frightened me.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular since you've been feeling this way?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really felt guilty about anything in particular. It's... mostly just feeling so slowed down and having those scary thoughts I mentioned. But no, I wouldn't say I feel guilty.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still since you started feeling this way?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. It's actually kind of the opposite. Like I was saying earlier, I just feel really slowed down. So, sitting still isn't an issue at all... it's getting up and moving that's the hard part for me right now.
Have you been feeling worthless since you started feeling this way?
No, not worthless. Just... tired and slow, like I said. But I don't feel like I'm a bad person or worthless or anything like that.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, I've probably lost a little weight. I know I should be eating regularly, especially right now, but... most days food just sounds really unappealing. It's getting to the point where I'll realize halfway through a clinic shift that I've only had some crackers or coffee all day. I just don't really have an appetite.
Have you experienced any strange thoughts or heard any voices that others couldn't hear since you've been feeling this way?
No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or had any weird thoughts. Just the low energy and not wanting to eat, really. My mind is pretty normal, just... tired.
Have you been thinking about death frequently since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, I have. Honestly, that's what scared me enough to finally say something about it at my prenatal appointment. I've been having these thoughts where... I just wish I wouldn't wake up. I don't have a plan to actually hurt myself or anything like that, but... yeah, the thoughts are there.
Have you been feeling fidgety or having an inability to sit still at any point since you started feeling this way?

No, not fidgety. It's actually the opposite. Everything I do just feels... slowed down. It's like I'm moving through syrup all day. Even simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound care supplies or just finishing up my charting, it's taking me noticeably longer than it should. I just feel so slow.
Have you been feeling agitated or irritable since you started feeling this way?

No, not really. I haven't noticed being irritable or agitated. Honestly, I don't think I even have the energy to get worked up or annoyed about things right now. It's really just that heavy, slow feeling I mentioned.
Have you been feeling like you're restless or can't sit still at any point since you started feeling this way?

No, like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm not restless at all. It's really the exact opposite. I just feel... completely slowed down. Like I'm moving through syrup. Even doing the really simple tasks at the clinic, um, like getting wound supplies together for a patient or just finishing up my charting... it's all taking me noticeably longer than it should. I just don't have any of that kind of restless energy, I'm just slow.
Have you been feeling like you can't sit still or have an intense urge to move around since you started feeling this way?

I... I think you just asked me that. But no, I don't have any urge to move around. Like I was just saying, it's the exact opposite for me. Everything I do just feels really slowed down, like I'm moving through syrup. Even the simple stuff at the clinic, like getting wound supplies together or finishing my charting, it all takes me noticeably longer than it should. I'm definitely not having trouble sitting still.
Have you been feeling like you need to pace back and forth or engage in other physical activity to relieve your emotional state?

No, definitely not. Um, I feel like we keep covering this, but I really don't have the energy to pace or do any kind of physical activity. Like I've been saying, I'm just completely slowed down, so I don't have any urge to do that.
Would you say your feelings of sadness are present most of the day or nearly every day?

Yeah, it's... it's definitely most of the day. Really, it's been nearly every day for the past few weeks. That's actually why I came in. I've just felt this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day long. Even when I'm at work, um, you know, smiling at the patients and trying to do my job, inside I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
Would you say your low mood is mildly, moderately, or severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

I would say... probably moderately. I mean, I’m still making it to work, so I am functioning on some level. But my supervisor has already noticed that my charting has been incomplete lately. And outside of work, I’ve just been pulling away from my friends and, you know, the things that usually keep me steady. So it's definitely having a real impact on my day-to-day life.
Would you describe your current feelings of sadness as being mildly, moderately, or severely distressing?

I'm not really sure how to rate that, honestly. Um... I haven't really thought about it in terms of mild, moderate, or severe distress. I just know it's really hard to deal with every day. So I don't know exactly where it falls on a scale like that, it's just a constant, heavy feeling that I want to go away.
Would you say your low mood is interfering with your ability to work, take care of things at home, or get along with others a little, a lot, or somewhere in between?

I guess I'd say somewhere in between. Um, like I was saying a minute ago, I am still showing up for my shifts, but it is interfering. My supervisor has already noticed that my charting is incomplete lately. And as for getting along with others... I'm just not really seeing anyone. I've been pulling away from my friends and stepping back from the things that usually keep me steady. So, yeah, it's definitely somewhere in the middle, maybe leaning toward a lot.
